content:
Dear all,

the PHP security vulnerability which even general media reported on forced us to do something about our nForum, which was written in PHP. The result is that we are experimenting with a new Zulip-based nForum.

Zulip was a canonical choice since several communities adjacent to ours are already using Zulip: see e.g. categorytheory.zulipchat.com, hott.zulipchat.com and leanprover.zulipchat.com.

This is an ephemeral test instance to gather feedback. It will be wiped and later rebuilt.

You can log in to this test instance by clicking on "Forgot your password?" and entering the mail address you were registered with at the old nForum. (Your old password will not work. You can also create a new account if you wish.) If you are unsure what your address was, or if you no longer have access to it (for instance because it was an old institutional address), please get in touch, at iblech-nlab@speicherleck.de or (preferably) +4917695110311 :-)

Perhaps the most important question you might have is: Where do I find the list of nLab's latest changes? Try "Recent conversations", or "Latest Changes > Go to channel feed", or "Latest Changes > Go to list of topics".

Right now, nLab edit announcements still go to the old (but currently closed) nForum, but the nLab integration with the Zulip nForum is already tested and ready to go. Links to the old nForum are transparently redirected to this one.

Cheers,
Ingo
subject: Zulip nForum

content:
Thank you for your report, Toby! For me, logging in is very fast, and also in general the Zulip nForum seems quite snappy. But of course I believe you with that experience. Can you do the following?

  1. Log out
  2. Open a new browser tab
  3. Open your browser's developer tools (Ctrl+Shift+I)
  4. Navigate to the Network tab
  5. Log in to the nForum
  6. Save the network trace as an HAR file
  7. Share this HAR file with me (privately, as it contains session cookies with which your session can be taken over)
subject: Zulip nForum

On the announcement mechanism: This used to drive the nForum discussions; people would make edits to the nLab and others would react to their edit announcements, and so on.

Hence I feel like without it we are not really testing the new nForum. Indeed, nForum activity (which was never high) has died out now, while people are silently editing the nLab.

Therefore I would say it's time to make the transition and bring the announcement mechanism back! If possible?

content:
Dear all, sorry for the uncertainty! When I wrote that message, I had the expectation that one or perhaps two days later the persistent Zulip nForum would be live. But then unfortunately various delays occurred.

If a final practice run goes well, then this evening we'll have a proper, non-ephemeral, Zulip nForum, complete with nLab integration. :-) And I believe that I can also carry, through the nuke-and-rebuild, the messages which have happened here in the meantime, and also your login information, so that you don't need to reset your account again.

Hopefully commenting can then resume, without uncertainty and with a speedy and more future-stable Zulip nForum :-)
